segments.t: After hearing the whole story, Nagiyev declares that while actors can eat anything for big money, he ate it for free—so Katya, Senya, Fedya, and Barinov will all work a month without pay.
Можем съесть всё что угодно, но за большие деньги.
Значит, ты, ты и ты в этом месяце работаете бесплатно.
Ты что хотел сказать? Нагиев оказал медвежью услугу.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
'We are actors.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'we' and finishing on 'actors'.
Можем съесть всё что угодно, но за большие деньги.
'We can eat anything at all, but for big money.' Notice how Russian expresses 'can' and 'money' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'For big money!' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'for' before landing on 'money'.
'I ate this for free today.' Dmitry Nagiyev anchors the line on 'I', while 'ate' completes the thought.
Значит, ты, ты и ты в этом месяце работаете бесплатно.
'So you, you, and you are working for free this month.' The grammar packs 'so' and 'for free' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Understood.' The grammar packs 'understood' and 'understood' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Dmitry Nagiyev answers right away.
'I almost forgot. You too.' The grammar packs 'almost' and 'also' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Can you imagine, they have three sous-chefs.' The meaning hinges on 'imagine' working together with 'sous-chef' in spoken Russian.
'Around a thousand people.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'around' and finishing on 'man'. Chef Barinov answers right away.
Ты что хотел сказать? Нагиев оказал медвежью услугу.
'What did you want to say? Nagiyev did us a disservice.' Chef Barinov addresses the listener with the informal singular 'you' alongside 'service'.
'Chef! Phone for you!' In Russian, the idea of 'Chef Barinov' flows naturally into 'phone' without extra filler words.
'Excuse me. Well go on, go.' Chef Barinov brings out the contrast between 'sorry' and 'come on' in a few short words. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
Можем съесть всё что угодно, но за большие деньги.
Значит, ты, ты и ты в этом месяце работаете бесплатно.
Ты что хотел сказать? Нагиев оказал медвежью услугу.
And that finishes Scene Thirteen. Listen for Nagiyev's punchline adding Barinov himself to the list of people working for free this month. Until next time!
